title: Hidden Gems on a Ring: Infant Massive Clusters and Their Formation Timeline Unveiled by ALMA, HST, and JWST in NGC 3351
question: Identify and characterize forming (embedded, infant) young massive clusters in the central starburst ring of NGC 3351 using matched-resolution ALMA, HST and JWST data, and infer their evolutionary timeline and large-scale context

data.sensitivity: Continuum 1-sigma ~6.5–6.8 uJy/beam (Band 3), ~80–100 uJy/beam (Band 7); line cubes 0.3–2.5 K per channel (see Table 2)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA visibilities into continuum maps and line cubes
recipe.method: Observatory-supplied calibration scripts and CASA pipeline; line and continuum subsets extracted, combined across array configurations and imaged with a modified PHANGS-ALMA imaging pipeline (two-stage tclean); primary-beam corrected, beams circularized, cubes converted to brightness temperature
key_parameters: Line cubes cut to +/-300 km/s around systemic velocity of 778 km/s
Channel widths: 10 km/s for HCN, HCO+, CS; native 0.85 km/s for CO(3-2) (also a 5 km/s version)
Clean depth: multiscale to S/N=4, then single-scale to S/N=1 (CO 3-2) or 2 (others)
Briggs robust 1.0; uniform weighting for CO(3-2)

recipe.method: Select peaks above S/N=5 in the 93 GHz and 350 GHz continuum images, merge counterparts, separate a blended pair by eye

recipe.goal: Measure continuum fluxes, sizes and line luminosities/widths of each source
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits with imfit inside circular apertures; elliptical apertures from the fits to extract spectra; local background annulus subtracted; line integrated flux and effective width measured using CO(3-2) as velocity prior
key_parameters: Circular aperture of diameter 0.34″ (twice the beam FWHM); imfit dooff=True; beam deconvolution attempted
Isolated-source background annuli: inner/outer radii 2x/3x aperture radii
assumptions: Line emission is spatially associated with thermal dust, so 350 GHz apertures are used where available

recipe.goal: Cross-match ALMA sources with HST clusters and JWST sources
recipe.method: HST class 1-2 clusters matched if within the ALMA source major-axis HWHM; JWST 3.35 micron catalog matched with the same criterion (closest if several), plus visual inspection of multi-band JWST images

recipe.goal: Derive gas masses from 350 GHz dust continuum
recipe.method: Two-component (dust + free-free) decomposition to check dust dominance at 350 GHz; optically thin dust optical depth tau350 = S350/(Omega B_nu(Tdust)); gas mass = tau350/(kappa350 D/G) x Omega d^2
assumptions: Optically thin dust (tau350 ~ 0.001–0.005); synchrotron ignored in dust/free-free split

recipe.goal: Derive stellar masses from 93 GHz free-free emission
recipe.method: Treat 93 GHz flux as free-free, convert to ionizing photon rate Q0 (Emig et al. 2020 formula), then to stellar mass with a Starburst99-based conversion M* = Q0 / 2.2e46 s^-1 Msun
key_parameters: Synchrotron spectral index -0.75 for MERLIN-based bound on synchrotron fraction
assumptions: 3 Myr old stellar population, Kroupa IMF, solar metallicity; negligible ionizing photon escape
Stellar age choice changes masses by 0.3–0.6 dex (zero age: 2x smaller; 5 Myr: 5x larger)

recipe.goal: Derive size, total mass, gas fraction, virial mass, escape velocity, free-fall time, gas surface density and Eddington ratio
recipe.method: Half-light radius from imfit; M_tot = M_gas + M_star; M_vir = 5 sigma^2 R_hl/(f G); v_esc = sqrt(2G(M_tot/3.4)/R_hl); rho_tot = (M_tot/3.4)/(4/3 pi R_hl^3) and t_ff = sqrt(3 pi/(32 G rho)); Sigma_gas = M_gas/(pi R_hl^2/ln2); Eddington ratio from Sigma_gas and f_gas
key_parameters: Virial geometric factor f = 5/3 (rho ~ r^-2); sigma from HCN(1-0) effective width
Psi ~ 1e3 Lsun/Msun for ages <~3 Myr (Starburst99, Kroupa IMF)
assumptions: Uniform gas sphere with central star cluster for the Eddington ratio

recipe.goal: Classify YMC candidates and infer an evolutionary timeline
recipe.method: Classify sources into four types from presence/absence at 350 GHz, 93 GHz, JWST and HST; compare number counts of ALMA YMCs and HST clusters (<10 Myr) in a matched mass range; durations proportional to counts and scaled to a 10 Myr reference window
assumptions: (1) SFR of the ring constant over 10 Myr; (2) combined ALMA+HST sample complete over matched mass range up to ~10 Myr; (3) no substantial YMC loss

recipe.goal: Place YMCs in ring context: SFR share, azimuthal trends, outflow energetics
recipe.method: Divide total YMC stellar mass by the 93 GHz-bright duration for an instantaneous SFR; examine azimuthal distribution vs ring models (popcorn vs pearls on a string); compare Starburst99 mechanical energy (with 2% retention) to reported outflow energies
assumptions: 4–6 Myr duration of the 93 GHz-bright phase

score_reason: Observation and analysis choices (S/N=5 detection, imfit, mass formulas and constants) are well specified and results are numeric, but imaging parameters, calibrator and line-free channels are not given and HST/JWST catalogs partly depend on in-preparation work
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA-only chain (continuum detection, imfit fluxes and sizes, gas and stellar masses, derived quantities) uses archival-type data and fully stated formulas with numeric tables to check; HST/JWST-dependent steps would need substitute catalogs
